newsitem.title: UK: Newspaper says poll could change UK election plan.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper says poll could change UK election plan.

text.p: A poll showing British Prime Minister John Major's ruling Conservatives will be defeated in a crucial by-election could force him to push forward the date of the general election, The Sun newspaper said on Monday.

The country's top-selling tabloid said a MORI poll shows the opposition Labour Party, which is widely tipped to win the general election that Major must call by May, will win the Wirral South constituency in northern England with a 16-point swing.
"No government has held office after suffering a swing of more than five percent in the last by-election," the newspaper said.
Major must choose a date for the by-election following the death of Conservative member of parliament Barry Porter last year. Porter won the seat in 1992 with a majority of 8,123.
The death of another Conservative, Ian Mills, last week pushed the government into a minority in parliament, with 323 opposition MPs facing 322 of Major's supporters.
It is the first minority government in Britain since 1979.
"Tory strategists believe the (by-election) setback will make him drop his chosen general election date -- May 1 -- and settle for March 20," The Sun said.
The newspaper, quoting strategists, predicted Major will abort the by-election and push up the general election date.
According to the MORI poll, 69 percent of those questioned are dissatisfied with the government. More than 60 percent of former Conservatives said they are fed up with the government.
Last week cabinet ministers dampened speculation about an early election saying May 1, the same day as local elections, was still Major's preferred date.
May 22 is technically the last possible date for an election.
